title: A Scholarship for the Recipe
premise: Quentin Thackeray, a scholarship student at Hollowmere Academy, has spent two years keeping her head down, counting days until graduation. When stern Chef Odile pairs her with her nemesis, golden-boy Julian Ashford, for a semester project recreating the school's legendary founding recipe, they unearth documents suggesting the recipe was stolen from a kitchen girl erased from the school's history. As their rivalry thaws into friendship, Quentin must choose between protecting Julian's family legacy and exposing the truth, culminating in a final audition where she tells the whole story publicly—costing her the friendship before it can truly begin, until Julian chooses truth too.
about_author: Vesper Villalobos is a former line cook who traded service windows for school libraries and now writes stories about kids who find families in unexpected places. She lives near the coast with her grandmother's recipe box and an opinionated cat named Roux.

chapters.title: Day Four Hundred and Twelve
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She maps her countdown to graduation, cataloguing the social strata of Hollowmere Academy and her place at its bottom rung. Establishes her invisibility strategy and her scholarship stakes. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Pairing Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Chef Odile announces semester partners for the Founders' Recipe project: Quentin and Julian Ashford, heir to the Ashford name on half the buildings. Their first clash in the teaching kitchen ends with flour on both uniforms. Beat: humiliation sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He resents being paired with the scholarship kid who once beat him in a bake-off, and drafts rules of engagement to keep the project impersonal. His father's expectations surface. Beat: pressure disguised as confidence.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Researching in the school archive, she finds a gap in the founding records—a cook listed only as 'the girl from the kitchens.' A librarian hints the original recipe came from somewhere else. Beat: first spark of curiosity overtaking survival instinct.

chapters.title: Sunday Shifts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced weekend lab sessions force actual conversation; Julian admits he hates business school plans made for him, Quentin admits she cooks to remember her late mother. Beat: grudging recognition of kinship.

chapters.title: The Ashford Version
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He brings his family's 'original' recipe card, but Quentin notices the handwriting doesn't match the era—and a fainter script underneath, scraped away. Beat: unease as legacy shows its seams.

chapters.title: Belonging, Briefly
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The project group—them plus two misfit classmates—shares midnight cooking sessions in the dorm kitchen. For one night Quentin feels part of something. Beat: warmth she doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She identifies the ghost cook: Rosa Ibáñez, whose name appears in a ledger then vanishes after a fire 'she' allegedly caused. The recipe was rebranded as Ashford property. Beat: righteous anger with personal resonance.

chapters.title: Don't Tell Him Yet
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Her new friends urge her to go public; she hesitates, knowing Julian's family funded her scholarship indirectly. First lie of omission to Julian. Beat: guilt curdling loyalty.

chapters.title: The Fire That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Investigating independently, Julian finds his great-grandfather's letters admitting the theft and blaming Rosa for his own negligence. He hides the letters. Beat: the corruption of inherited power touching him personally.

chapters.title: Two Secrets, One Kitchen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both work on the audition dish while concealing what they know; tension leaks into every shared task until a burned batch becomes a shouting match. Beat: intimacy weaponized by secrecy.

chapters.title: Midterm Tasting
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Chef Odile critiques their dish as technically perfect and emotionally hollow, unknowingly diagnosing them both. Julian watches Quentin deflect and wonders what she's carrying. Beat: exposed nerve.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. With the librarian's help, Quentin locates Rosa's descendants' contact in an old parish record. She drafts a letter, then locks it in her drawer instead. Beat: courage deferred, self-betrayal acknowledged.

chapters.title: Father Knows Best
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. His father announces the audition will be filmed for the Ashford centennial campaign, turning the project into propaganda. Julian realizes his discovery would destroy everything his father built—including him. Beat: fear wearing obedience.

chapters.title: Caught Between
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A classmate leaks that Quentin has been digging into Rosa Ibáñez; Julian confronts her, feeling betrayed that she investigated his family behind his back. Beat: the friendship fractures along the fault line of trust.

chapters.title: Cold Station
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They complete required sessions in hostile silence, communicating only through the dish itself. Both secretly refine the recipe toward Rosa's recovered version. Beat: grief expressed as craft.

chapters.title: Rosa's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin finally sends the letter; Rosa's granddaughter Marisol visits, sharing family recipes passed down orally—the true foundation of the Founders' Recipe. She asks only to be remembered, not avenged. Beat: purpose clarified beyond winning.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Quentin offers Julian co-authorship of the truth; his father simultaneously threatens to have Quentin's scholarship reviewed if the story surfaces. Julian stalls, torn. Beat: the cost of power made explicit.

chapters.title: What Friendship Costs
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Julian, cornered, publicly disavows the research to protect his father, calling Quentin's claims 'a misunderstanding.' The found-family group splinters; Quentin stands alone. Beat: heartbreak as the price of integrity.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Before judges, donors, and cameras, Quentin presents the dish and tells Rosa's full story, naming names, risking expulsion and her scholarship. Silence, then Marisol stands and speaks. Beat: terror transfigured into testimony.

chapters.title: The Recipe Renamed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fallout: the school launches an inquiry, the recipe is officially credited to Rosa Ibáñez, and Quentin's scholarship is converted to a fund bearing Rosa's name. Julian's father rages; Julian moves out. Beat: justice incomplete but real.

chapters.title: Table for Five
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Weeks later, Julian appears at the dorm kitchen door with Rosa's restored recipe card and an apology he doesn't dress up. The friend group reconvenes over a imperfect, honest batch. Graduation countdown now counts toward something. Beat: belonging chosen, not granted.
